classification.difficultyReason: Requires finding an intermediate angle, checking supplementary possibilities and rounding the resulting angles to the nearest minute.

content.prompt: Find the possible values of $\theta$ in this diagram, correct to the nearest minute.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with upper-left, lower-left and right vertices. Preserve the source orientation, side labels and interior angle-label placement; no vertex names or additional angle marks are printed.
spec.mathematics: The upper-left–lower-left side is 12. The lower-left–right side is 15. The right angle is 35 degrees 24 minutes, and theta is at the lower-left vertex. The sketch depicts theta as obtuse but supplies no explicit obtuse-angle restriction.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown theta appear; numerical answers and auxiliary angle names are excluded.

inlines.text: . Both satisfy the angle-sum check; the supplied key gives the obtuse possibility only.

answer.worked:
Let $\alpha$ be the unlabelled upper-left angle.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\alpha}{15}&=\frac{\sin(35^{\circ}24')}{12}\\\sin\alpha&=\frac{15\sin(35^{\circ}24')}{12}\\\alpha_1&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{15\sin(35^{\circ}24')}{12}\right)\\\alpha_2&=180^{\circ}-\alpha_1\end{align*}$$
Both possibilities are valid: $\alpha_1+35^{\circ}24'\approx81.79^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$ and $\alpha_2+35^{\circ}24'\approx169.01^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$.
Using the unrounded angles,
$$\begin{align*}\theta_1&=180^{\circ}-35^{\circ}24'-\alpha_1\\\theta_1&\approx98^{\circ}12'\\\theta_2&=180^{\circ}-35^{\circ}24'-\alpha_2\\\theta_2&\approx11^{\circ}00'\end{align*}$$
The supplied answer $98^{\circ}12'$ is the obtuse possibility shown by the sketch.
